get.description:
Returns the operation row plus its per-step progress events. Clients poll this endpoint while `done` is false; when `done` flips true, `response` may carry the typed result (`SUCCEEDED`) and `error.message` carries a failure reason when available. Prefer `POST /v1/operations/{id}:wait` for sync "wait until done" semantics - it long-polls server-side instead of asking the client to tight-poll.

Native Install details come directly from their selected Workflow execution; legacy catalog projections may lag execution. Terminal outcomes remain immutable.

post.description:
Long-polls server-side until the operation reaches a terminal state (`SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`) or the timeout elapses. Returns the latest `Operation` either way - check `done` to distinguish.

Native Install references are read from their selected Workflow execution with a bounded server-side wait. Legacy operations retain their existing catalog subscription. A wait timeout returns the latest snapshot and does not cancel execution.

Native Install details come directly from their selected Workflow execution; legacy catalog projections may lag execution. Terminal outcomes remain immutable.

post.description:
Requests cancellation of an in-flight operation. Cancellation is asynchronous: successful requests return the current operation envelope while the worker drains the current step before settling into a terminal result. Replaying the request with the same Idempotency-Key is supported. If the operation has already reached a terminal state, cancellation is rejected with Unprocessable Entity.

When accepted, the operation is not cancelled instantly; it transitions through the normal cancellation flow and may still report progress for a short time.

post.description: Snapshots the whole sandbox, including its files and the memory of running processes, and stops it, returning an Operation. A suspended sandbox costs only storage. Requires `manage`. While suspended, commands, file operations, terminals and previews are unavailable; ports and preview URLs stop answering until it is resumed.
